posts.headline: Hitmen Face the Toughest Road Left in Archie's League
posts.body: Hitmen, Killers and SeaBirds have the gnarliest roads ahead, while RailRoaders catch a breather.
content:
Hitmen own the toughest road left, with difficulty 68 and remaining opponents averaging 149.7 PPG.

Killers (66) and SeaBirds (66) are right behind, and nobody in this league wants that gauntlet.

RailRoaders have the easiest path, difficulty 32, opponents averaging just 120.3 PPG.

See every team's road in the Gauntlet rankings, and if you think your schedule is rough, the trade builder might be your way out.

posts.headline: Week 11 Doubleheader: Nomads, Islanders and Freeze Feel the Heat
posts.body: Every franchise plays twice this week. Islanders vs Deadly leads the slate, the Chickens look untouchable, and the bubble is tight. Here is what to watch and who I like.
content: Notes from around the league: this is a doubleheader week, so every franchise plays two games and each one counts on its own. Check the live scoreboard all day, because a swept week and a split week look very different in the standings.
The playoff race is tight. Plenty of teams sit within reach of the cutoff, and the tiebreakers will matter. Keep an eye on the standings as the games finish.

story: This is the Game of the Week, and the stakes are lopsided. Deadly are at 81 percent playoff odds, and a win pushes them to about 89 percent.
The Islanders are at 0 percent, so this one is about pride and spoiling someone else's week. Their history is close, with the Islanders up 4-3 since 2024.
Watch the QB spots. Bo Nix and Jordan Love project strong numbers for Deadly, while Bryce Young and Aaron Rodgers carry the Islanders.
The key NFL game is BAL at CAR, which projects 62.7 points from these starters, so Jacoby Brissett and Bryce Young decide it.
My pick: Deadly, 157-150.
Wolverines are at 54 percent and riding a two-game streak. Roughnecks have lost five straight and are out.
The key NFL game is JAX at NYG, where Trevor Lawrence and Parker Washington carry the Wolverines.
My pick: Wolverines, 150-123.
Kraken are at 65 percent and riding a bubble edge, while Kung Fu sit at 2 percent. Jayden Daniels leads the Kraken projection.
My pick: Kraken, 160-151.
Goats are at 60 percent and in control of the race. Nordics have lost eight straight and are out at 0 percent.
My pick: Goats, 154-124.
Nomads are at 60 percent and riding a four-game win streak. Maddogs are at 11 percent and need a miracle.
Tyler Shough and Caleb Williams make the key NFL game, Nomads' QBs against the Bears' offense.
My pick: Nomads, 152-141.
Kraken lead the all-time series 2-0 and have won the last two meetings. Tikis are effectively out at 0 percent.
My pick: Kraken, 158-127.
SnakeEyes and Dawgs are almost identical at 43 and 44 percent, so this is a coin flip with big consequences.
The key NFL game is MIN at SF, where Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey decide it.
My pick: SnakeEyes, 137-135.
Nomads have won the last two meetings and lead the series 2-1, at 60 percent playoff odds. Phantoms are at 13 percent.
My pick: Nomads, 151-128.
BearCats have won nine straight and sit at 67 percent. Veterans are out, with four straight losses.
My pick: BearCats, 147-127.
Badgers hold 59 percent playoff odds and have dropped two straight, so a win matters. Bears are out of it at 0 percent.
My pick: Badgers, 147-139.
The Chickens are at 100 percent playoff odds and riding a 17-game streak. Freeze need this one more, sitting at 41 percent.
Jared Goff leads the Chickens' projection, and Bucky Irving and Jameson Williams give Freeze a shot.
My pick: Chickens, 168-152.
Tombstones are locked in at 100 percent, but Wolverines are at 54 percent and a win moves them toward 71.
Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence are the swing players here.
My pick: Wolverines, 149-146.

closing: Broadcast guide: the two NFL games to watch are BAL at CAR and JAX at NYG, which swing multiple matchups.
Lock in your lineup before kickoff, and check the live scoreboard throughout the day.

posts.headline: Luchadors and Foxes complete 4-asset trade
posts.body: League sources tell me the Luchadors and Foxes have agreed to a blockbuster swap! The Luchadors are receiving QB, Bryce Young and RB, Chase Brown, while the Foxes are landing QB, Jared Goff and RB, Jonah Coleman. Boom! The deal is official and the rosters are about to look very different.
posts.analysis: Luchadors get a B+ here: Bryce Young offers real upside and Chase Brown brings a strong dynasty floor at running back. Foxes earn a B- since Jared Goff gives them immediate stability, but Jonah Coleman doesn't move the needle enough to fully justify giving up the young upside.

posts.headline: Chickens and Sioux complete 4-asset trade
posts.body: I'm told the Chickens and Sioux have agreed to a blockbuster dynasty deal! League sources tell me the Chickens are receiving QB Cam Ward and WR Amon-Ra St. Brown, while the Sioux are landing QB Jayden Daniels and WR Malik Nabers. Boom! Two contenders just reshuffled their rosters in a big way.
posts.analysis: Sioux get the edge here with Jayden Daniels and Malik Nabers giving them a higher ceiling for the next several seasons, earning them a B+. The Chickens get a grade of B- for Amon-Ra St. Brown's steady production, though they're banking on Cam Ward developing into the elite option they need.

posts.headline: Tombstones trade with Razerbacks for WR, Jameson Williams
posts.body: League sources tell me the Tombstones and Razerbacks have agreed to a blockbuster swap, and I'm told it's official. Tombstones are landing WR, Jameson Williams, while the Razerbacks are bringing in WR, Josh Downs. Boom! Two wideouts changing hands in a deal that has the whole league buzzing.
posts.analysis: Williams brings big-play upside that the Tombstones can use right now, and Downs gives the Razerbacks a reliable target in the slot. I'm giving this one a B+ across the board, with a slight edge to the Razerbacks for landing the more consistent producer.

posts.headline: Week 10 Doubleheader: Mafia-Terminators Leads the Slate
posts.body: Every franchise plays twice this week, and the Mafia-Terminators rivalry headlines a loaded Saturday slate. Here is what to watch, who I like, and where the NFL games decide everything.
content: Boom! It's Week 10 in Archie's Fantasy Football League, and every franchise plays two games, so this is a doubleheader weekend that will make or break playoff hopes.
Track every score on the live scoreboard and check the standings to see how one result can swing your playoff odds.

story: Money is nice, but championships are better, and this is the Game of the Week: Mafia at Terminators.
The all-time series is dead even at 2-2, and I'm told this one is personal.
Mafia carries roughly 60% playoff odds into this game, and a win pushes that to about 71%.
Aaron Rodgers and Ja'Marr Chase give Mafia a huge edge, and the Terminators need Justin Herbert and Brock Bowers to produce.
The NFL swing game is PIT at CIN, where Rodgers and Chase on one side meet the Bengals defense on the other.
My pick: Mafia. Their projected 176.7 is too much for Terminators' 126.5.
Mafia's 60% playoff odds are on the line against the Wizards, who sit at roughly 12%.
Jayden Daniels is the lone star on the Wizards side, and Mafia has Bo Nix and Caleb Williams.
My pick: Mafia, and they should not be close.
Dawgs can help their own cause here against a Stonecutters team at roughly 1% playoff odds.
Joe Burrow is the one name that matters on the Stonecutters side.
My pick: Dawgs.
Monsters are already all but in at 14-4, so this one is about seeding, not survival.
Foxes need the win, with Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown carrying the NFL swing game PIT at CIN.
My pick: Foxes in a shootout, though Joe Burrow gives Monsters the edge.
Hawks are at 1% playoff odds, and I'm told they are playing for pride now.
Dawgs hold a 1-0 series lead and roughly 40% playoff odds.
My pick: Dawgs, with Dak Prescott and Trey McBride giving them the edge.
Assassins at roughly 56% against a Stingers team fighting for relevance.
Dak Prescott is the difference maker in this one.
My pick: Assassins.
Roos have a chance to take advantage of a 3-15 Chupacabras team that has lost 14 straight.
Derrick Henry is Chupacabras' best option.
My pick: Roos, and it should not be close.
Tigers are fighting for their season at about 51%, while Sandmen are reeling on a three-game skid.
Jared Goff and Trey McBride are Sandmen's best hope.
My pick: Tigers, with Brock Purdy carrying them through the SFO at DAL game.
BearCats have won seven straight, but they only have 9-9 to show for it.
Waves are on a three-game streak with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb leading the way.
The SFO at DAL game decides this one, with McCaffrey on one side and Prescott and Purdy on the other.
My pick: Waves, 141.4 to 129.0 on the projections.
Assassins are sitting at roughly 56% and have to take care of business against Phantoms.
Dak Prescott and Trevor Lawrence give Assassins firepower Phantoms cannot match.
My pick: Assassins.
Tikis have lost five straight, and Roos are at about 45% playoff odds.
Roos have Dak Prescott and Tyler Shough, which is a lot of firepower.
My pick: Roos, in what should be a comfortable win.
Foxes sit at about 44% and have won three straight, while Luchadors hold roughly 12% odds.
Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs lead the Luchadors, but Ja'Marr Chase and Chase Brown give Foxes the edge.
My pick: Foxes.

closing: Watch PIT at CIN closely, because Ja'Marr Chase and Joe Burrow decide several of these matchups.
Keep an eye on SFO at DAL too, since Dak Prescott and Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey all play key roles across the league.
